topic: Coordination as a diagnostic of wordhood
claim: Passing any one of the coordination or modification tests suffices for a composite nominal.
evidence_summary: CGEL admits coordinated bases inside compounds and allows washing-machine to pass by reanalysis.
finding: Successful coordination alone cannot choose between base coordination and syntactic reanalysis. A compound of another type is a calibration case.
inference: Does a positive coordination test identify a syntactic nominal when compound-base coordination is available?

evidence.source: U.S. Census Bureau (May 2008). Changes in the Relationship Categories Between 2007 & 2008.
evidence.passage: §14.4, p. 449. Passing any one of the coordination or modification tests suffices for a composite nominal.
evidence.example: The enumeration uses brothers- and sisters-in-law, preserving the characteristic internal plural.
evidence.establishes: A calibration case for coordination within another type of compound. It does not by itself settle the analysis of washing-machine.
